slides.title: Scientific Exchange Is Not Promotion
bullets: A genuine, balanced, non-promotional dialogue about science
Regulators and codes of practice treat it as a distinct category
That protection only holds if the conversation meets real conditions

slides.title: It Must Be Scientifically Balanced
bullets: Present favourable and unfavourable data alike
Acknowledge the real limitations of the evidence
Not just the parts that support the product

slides.title: It Must Be Genuinely Scientific in Purpose
bullets: Responsive to the physician's question or a legitimate scientific reason
Never driven by a commercial calendar or sales target
Off-label discussion must follow local legal and company framework

slides.title: It Must Be Documented Accurately
bullets: Accurate documentation matters for compliance
It also ensures the insight generated isn't lost

slides.title: A Two-Way Exchange, Not a Presentation
bullets: MSL brings trial data, mechanism of action and disease-state expertise
Physician brings real-world experience and unanticipated questions
A conversation where only the MSL talks is a presentation, not exchange
Best MSLs treat every exchange as a chance to ask a useful question

slides.title: Balance and Purpose Keep It Credible
bullets: Techniques for running it well are covered in detail in Module 4
It's structured, principled communication with real boundaries
Staying inside those boundaries keeps Medical Affairs credible and compliant

takeaway.title: Scientific exchange is a protected, two-way dialogue with real boundaries
bullets: It must be balanced, genuinely scientific in purpose, and documented
It works only when the physician talks as much as the MSL does
Those boundaries are what keep the entire role credible and compliant
